command.short: Ask Jev a choice or score question and get a typed outcome
command.long:
jev-decide puts a choice (ask) or an ordered rubric (score) to TypeSafe AI's Jev model.
The outcome is decided, uncertain or escalate, and only a decided outcome is one to act on.
eval measures how well the confidence separates clear decisions from contested ones.
Exit codes: 0 decided, 10 uncertain, 11 escalate, 1 to 4 failures; eval exits 0 with a report.

commands.short: Ask Jev to choose between options
commands.long:
ask puts a choice question to Jev and prints the outcome as a JSON envelope.
Only a decided outcome has a choice; the other two name a leading option only.
Output schema_version: 2. Exit codes: 0 decided, 10 uncertain, 11 escalate.
commands.example:
jev-decide ask --spec decision.json
  jev-decide ask --state "all tests passed" --instructions "Ship it?" --option ship="safe to release" --option hold=wait

commands.short: Generate the autocompletion script for bash
commands.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(jev-decide completion bash)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	jev-decide completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/jev-decide

#### macOS:

	jev-decide completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/jev-decide

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

commands.short: Generate the autocompletion script for zsh
commands.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

	echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(jev-decide completion zsh)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	jev-decide completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_jev-decide"

#### macOS:

	jev-decide completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_jev-decide

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

commands.short: Measure how well Jev's confidence separates clear decisions from contested ones
commands.long:
eval asks Jev one choice question per decision in a labelled set and reports
accuracy, contested AUC, Brier score and precision and recall per threshold.
It measures; it never approves. Both files are validated before any request.
Output schema_version: 2. Exit code 0 when the report is printed.
commands.example:
jev-decide eval --decisions testdata/decisions.json --truth testdata/decisions_truth.json
  jev-decide eval --decisions past.json --truth past_truth.json --cache-dir .eval-cache

commands.short: Ask Jev to rate content against an ordered rubric
commands.long:
score rates the state against ordered levels and prints the outcome as a JSON envelope.
Only a decided outcome has a level; the other two name the nearest level only.
Output schema_version: 2. Exit codes: 0 decided, 10 uncertain, 11 escalate.
commands.example:
jev-decide score --spec incident.json
  jev-decide score --state "checkout fails for half of users" --level minor="cosmetic" --level major="cannot buy"
